entries.original_authors: Prasada, S.; Khemlani, S.; Leslie, S.; Glucksberg, S.
entries.description: Principled connections between kinds and properties license self-referential generalizations, whereas non-principled connections do not.
entries.citation_sentence: [47] introduced several linguistic tests to distinguish principled from non-principled connections.
entries.notes: Experiment 1 adapted the self-referential generalization test from the original study to teleological generics.

entries.original_authors: Prasada, S.; Khemlani, S.; Leslie, S.; Glucksberg, S.
entries.description: Principled connections establish norms of normality and normativity for the properties of a kind, whereas non-principled connections do not.
entries.citation_sentence: As [47] point out, there are two ways of examining norm-based expectations.
entries.notes: Experiment 2a tested normality and normativity formulations as an extension of the original norm test.

entries.original_authors: Prasada, S.; Khemlani, S.; Leslie, S.; Glucksberg, S.
entries.description: Principled connections establish normative expectations that a kind should possess the corresponding property.
entries.citation_sentence: As [47] point out, there are two ways of examining norm-based expectations.
entries.notes: Experiment 2b used an alternative should formulation to extend the original normativity test.

entries.original_authors: Prasada, S.; Khemlani, S.; Leslie, S.; Glucksberg, S.
entries.description: Properties linked to a kind by a principled connection are construed as an aspect of that kind, whereas properties linked non-principally are not.
entries.citation_sentence: When a principled connection is present between a kind and a property, people construe the property as an aspect of the kind.
entries.notes: The paragraph identifies the aspect test as originating in the prior principled-connections work, cited as [47].

entries.original_authors: Prasada, S.; Khemlani, S.; Leslie, S.; Glucksberg, S.
entries.description: Principled connections license natural formal explanations that explain a property by reference to the kind, whereas non-principled connections do not.
entries.citation_sentence: Principled connections should license formal explanations, i.e., explanations that explain properties by referring to the kind in question [44].
entries.notes: Experiment 4 adapted the formal-explanations test to teleological phenomena; the sentence cites [44] directly, while the broader four-test framework is attributed to [47].
